title: Normalized scalar module transport for a supplied coefficient isomorphism
statement: Let l be prime, and let theta_X be a monoid-object isomorphism from the condensed coefficient pulled to each scheme X to the native locally finite-span function sheaf. Assume the coefficient pushforward square commutes for every scheme morphism. Then there exists the Data of def-sf-finite-span-module-comparison-data with exactly this theta, satisfying coefficient_sections, rho_composition, ordinary_mate, push_identity, underlying, finiteFree_sections, pushComposition_sections, pullComposition_mate, ordinary_composition, K-injective preservation in both directions, derived_push_normalization and field_normalization. The input theta need not satisfy a finite-field chart normalization. The inverse coefficient square and rho invertibility are proved separately by adjunction transposition and are not part of this conclusion. No exchange assertion is included.

proof.text: Use the input ring isomorphisms theta and their assumed direct-image coefficient square. Put $B_T$ for the reconstructed section-ring sheaf of $A_T$, and identify it with $A_T$ when writing ring maps. The assumed square says that the adjunct coefficient map $A_W\to v_*A_Z$ and the precomposition map $\mathcal R_W\to v_*\mathcal R_Z$ commute with $c_W$ and $v_*c_Z$. Taking adjuncts gives $c_Z\alpha_v=\rho_v v^{-1}c_W$. By sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients, $\alpha_v$ is an isomorphism; hence $\rho_v=c_Z\alpha_v(v^{-1}c_W)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. For composable $v:Z\to W$, $u:W\to T$, precomposing functions twice is precomposing with the composite projection. This holds before sheafification, hence also after it, and proves the composition identity for $\rho$ under the canonical inverse-image compositor. The same identity for $\alpha$ follows from its definition as the pullback-from-the-point comparison in sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms. Thus the displayed coefficient squares respect composition.

proof.text: Let $J_T$ be the internal-to-section equivalence of def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence. For a $B_T$-module $M$, define $S_TM$ by the same abelian sheaf and action $r\cdot_{S_T}m=c_T^{-1}(r)\cdot_M m$. Its inverse sends an $\mathcal R_T$-module $N$ to the action $a\cdot n=c_T(a)\cdot_N n$; both functors keep every arrow and restriction map. The two composites are the identity on actions as well. Set $E_T=S_TJ_T$. The equivalence $J_T$ is additive exact by lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport; $S_T$ preserves kernels and cokernels since their underlying abelian sheaves and induced actions are unchanged, using the kernel/cokernel description of def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category. Hence $E_T$ and its inverse are exact. A finite free trivialization $M|_U\cong A_T|_U^{\oplus n}$ is sent to a trivialization with $\mathcal R_T|_U^{\oplus n}$: the basis correspondence is coordinatewise $c_T$. This works also for rank zero and on every local trivializing object, with identical restrictions.

proof.text: Use lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport to compare the internal operations with the ordinary $B$-module operations and their specified ordinary adjunction. Write $\beta_v:B_W\to v_*B_Z$ and $\gamma_v:\mathcal R_W\to v_*\mathcal R_Z$ for their coefficient maps. Step 1 gives $c_Z\beta_v=\gamma_v c_W$ on the appropriate sections. Thus on $v_*M$, the two candidate $\mathcal R_W$-actions agree: the action through $\beta_v(c_W^{-1}r)$ equals that through $c_Z^{-1}(\gamma_v r)$. Identity on the underlying abelian sheaf is therefore the required direct-image comparison. Pullback over $B$ is inverse image with action transported by $\alpha_v^{-1}$, and pullback over $\mathcal R$ uses $\rho_v^{-1}$. Inverting step 1 gives $v^{-1}(c_W^{-1})\rho_v^{-1}=\alpha_v^{-1}c_Z^{-1}$, so these two actions agree too. The resulting pullback comparison is the identity on underlying inverse-image abelian sheaves. Equivalently, the tensor presentation of the ringed pullback collapses by $r\otimes m\mapsto\rho_v^{-1}(r)m$; its inverse is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. This also proves exactness of both pullbacks, using the exactness in sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients.

proof.text: The ordinary transposition for section modules sends a linear map out of $v^*M$ to its underlying abelian inverse-image/direct-image transpose; in its tensor presentation it first evaluates at $1\otimes m$. The comparisons in step 3 keep these abelian maps and $1\otimes m$ unchanged, so the two Hom bijections are equal. By lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport the internal Hom bijection is already the $B$-module one. Hence the ordinary units and counits, which are transposes of identity maps, agree after $E$. Retain the geometric direct-image compositor and its inverse-image mate specified in def-pd-section-module-operations-data. On sections the geometric compositor is the canonical identification between iterated and single base change of a test object. Relabelling scalars by $c$ preserves it by step 1; equality of the just-verified Hom bijections then preserves its mate, the inverse-image compositor. This proves the claimed ordinary adjunction and composition normalizations, not merely isomorphism of the endpoint functors.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization to $E_T$ and its exact inverse. The termwise functors carry quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and their inverse identities give inverse equivalences on the unbounded derived categories. They preserve chain homotopies: applying an additive functor to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same equation. For an acyclic complex $N$ on the target side and a K-injective $I$ on the source side, full faithfulness gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(N,E_TI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(E_T^{-1}N,I)=0$, since $E_T^{-1}N$ is acyclic by exactness. The criterion in def-pur-kinjective-complex proves preservation of K-injectivity; interchanging the two functors proves reflection and preservation by the inverse. In particular, they carry every K-injective resolution to a K-injective resolution.

proof.text: The small-site hypothesis allows prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist for the section-module categories; step 5 transports these resolutions internally. For a complex $K$ choose $K\to I$ K-injective. Compute $Rv_*^A K$ on $v_*^A I$, and $Rv_*^{\mathcal R}E_ZK$ on $v_*^{\mathcal R}E_ZI$, since $E_ZI$ is K-injective. The ordinary direct-image comparison of step 3 gives the isomorphism $D(E_W)Rv_*^A K\cong Rv_*^{\mathcal R}D(E_Z)K$ on these representatives. For a derived morphism, lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation represents it by the unique homotopy class between the chosen K-injective resolutions and computes its derived direct image by applying the ordinary functor to that class. Naturality of step 3 therefore proves naturality of this comparison. The same node's canonical transition maps between resolutions prove independence of the choices and compatibility with the right-derived comparison transformations. This proves a comparison of total right derived functors on arbitrary unbounded complexes, rather than separate cohomology isomorphisms.

proof.text: Now impose the stated finite-type scheme setting. Apply lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization with the condensed ring $C$ and reconstructed section rings $B_T$. It identifies the independently derived internal and $B$-module adjunctions, their units, counits and pullback compositors. It remains to relabel $B$ by $c$. Let $L$ be any complex and $I$ K-injective. The ordinary exact pullback $P=v_{\mathcal R}^*$ and its right adjoint $G=v_*^{\mathcal R}$ satisfy $\operatorname{Hom}_K(N,GI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(PN,I)=0$ for acyclic $N$, so $GI$ is K-injective. Thus lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived identifies both sides of the derived adjunction with homotopy classes of ordinary maps $PL\to I$ and $L\to GI$. Their bijection is exactly ordinary chain transposition: the ordinary Hom bijection commutes with differentials and homotopies, and on the $B$ side the canonical derived adjunction identified by lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization is the one derived from the ordinary adjunction, whose counit by lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived is induced by the ordinary counit; since the pullback is exact its derived comparison is invertible on every complex, and the comparison for the direct image is invertible on the K-injective $I$, so the derived transpose of the class of $h:L\to v_*I$ is the class of $\varepsilon_I\circ v^*h$, the ordinary transpose. Step 4 preserves that bijection under $S$, and step 6 identifies its right-derived comparison on $I$. Hence the relabelled derived Hom bijection sends the class of each chain map to the class of its ordinary transpose, as required. Every derived map into $I$ has such a representative by the cited Hom theorem, so this is equality on all morphisms. Identity transposes give equal units and counits. The localized geometric pullback compositors agree by step 4 and exact localization. This establishes the specified derived adjunction, not an adjunction chosen by transport.
